items.content:
Bloomberg’s chief Apple correspondent Mark Gurman on Siri, Tim Cook’s legacy, and what to expect from new CEO John Ternus.

Today, I’m talking with Mark Gurman, who is the world’s best-sourced Apple reporter — both as Bloomberg ’s chief Apple correspondent and the host of the upcoming podcast Power On .

Earlier this month, Apple hosted its annual iPhone hardware event, virtually every detail of which was reported ahead of time by Mark. But this event was special, for a number of reasons.

It was new Apple CEO John Ternus’ first major product launch since he took over for former CEO Tim Cook less than two weeks prior. It was also the debut of the iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable smartphone. The timing of those two things was not at all coincidental, as you’ll hear Mark explain. Apple takes these hardware events — and the stories they tell — extremely seriously.

This year’s story actually says a great deal about what’s happening at Apple, how Cook managed in wholesale leadership ranks over the past year, and how all of that might change Apple’s culture. Furthermore, what all that tells about Ternus’ plan to navigate Apple from what you might call the iPhone era into the AI era.

Okay: Bloomberg ’s Mark Gurman on the future of Apple. Here we go.

This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity.

Mark Gurman, you’re the chief Apple correspondent and the managing editor of consumer technology at Bloomberg . Welcome to Decoder .

Good to be here finally. Thanks for having me. And it’s been a while, so it’s good to catch up on all things Apple.

Yeah, I’m really excited to talk to you. Obviously, Apple just had its big event. They announced the iPhone Duo. It was John Ternus’s first event as CEO. This is a Decoder episode, so we’ve got a new CEO, and we’ve got a new org chart inside of Apple.

There’s been a lot of shuffling. You’ve been chronicling them very, very deeply over the past few years. Let’s just start with the event. I have a very basic question for you.

Do you ever get nostalgic for a time when you didn’t know what was going to happen at the iPhone event?

Do I ever get nostalgic?

Do you ever wish that you, Mark Gurman, were about to be surprised?

Honestly, I never think about it that way. I’m just fixated on delivering the goods and delivering the news. And people love their Apple. People want to know everything that’s coming down to the last minute, so I’m here to provide it for them.

The thing with me, and I don’t know if most people know this about me, but I hope people know this about me, is that I’m a huge Apple fan through and through, and I’ve always been. And I’m so lucky to be able to cover a company that I love, a company that I am obsessed with, and a company whose products I use. There are so many people who cover companies that they couldn’t care less about. That’s not me.

So I do what I do because I love Apple and I love covering Apple. I love the community around it, and I love talking about it. And it’s always fun to get a peek at the future and help keep not only myself informed, but people informed around me.

That actually leads me to a lot of things because I’ve known you forever. We’ve been working in and around the same spaces forever. You got your start as an Apple blogger at the Apple rumor sites.

There’s a whole culture around Apple that has grown up and changed over the years, and you can trace it to different eras of hardware, to different CEOs, to different sizes of the company. This was the first event with John Ternus as CEO. Apple announced a big new product in the iPhone Duo.

Do you sense that the community is changing? How do you think that community has changed over the years? And do you think Ternus is going to lead to a difference in what that community feels like?

I have to say, this event really didn’t feel much different than a Tim Cook event. They felt pretty interchangeable. It could have been Tim up there introducing it. It could have been Ternus up there introducing it.

The one thing I will say that did feel slightly different is that Ternus came out swinging with a point of view on AI. The first thing he came out with was about the intelligent personal hub. Now, here’s the big difference between Tim Cook and John Ternus in terms of their management style. You’re inside Apple, you’re an executive, you’ll come to him with an idea, you’ll come to him with a viewpoint, a decision, an opinion, and he’ll just pepper you with more questions. He won’t make a singular decision in many cases. It’s very much communal decision-making, collaborative decision-making.

John Ternus, if you come to him and you want him to make a decision, he’ll make a decision. He’ll have an opinion. Now, you may hate his opinion; you may completely disagree with him, but he has a viewpoint. But that’s the big difference between talking to people about Ternus and Tim.

Ternus comes out talking about his view on AI. I may disagree with it. A lot of people may disagree with it. They may think the OpenAI or Anthropic approach is superior, but at least he came out and had a viewpoint.

Apple’s been at this AI game now for two years since they launched Apple Intelligence at WWDC in 2024, and it’s been a mishmash of things. They haven’t really come out with a very strong narrative and viewpoint, and they finally did. So, as I said, whether you agree with it or not, they did do that. And I thought that was a really interesting way to kick off the keynote.

All right, we’re just going to get into the weeds of Apple nerds disagreeing about things.

I sat through that event, and I appreciated the same thing that you saw, which is, “Oh, we’re telling a story.” John Ternus is on the stage, and the first thing he’s doing is telling a story about this product and how it fits into the universe of technology. And then I took a beat, and I was like, oh, but they’re also just making sure that he’s successful at his first event by playing Apple’s greatest hits.

items.title: Corridor raises $25M seed to build a health benefits brokerage for SMBs
items.summary: Corridor focuses on SMBs, which it says traditional brokerages often overlook because small accounts generate lower commissions than larger accounts.
items.content:
It’s been a while since Jackson Wagner left his job as a product lead at Scale AI in July 2022. Now, he’s building in a new space altogether: The new effort is an AI health benefits brokerage called Corridor that focuses on small businesses, which it says traditional brokerages often overlook because small accounts generate lower commissions even though they take the same amount of time as larger accounts.

Corridor is betting an AI solution may help on that front. On its platform, customers work with human advisors while AI agents do administrative tasks in the background. The company says its agents can handle tedious office work like checking whether a doctor is in a customer’s insurance network, scheduling care, or providing a doctor updated health insurance information.

“We are every single employee and management’s concierge for all things healthcare,” Nikhil Aggarwal, the company’s CEO, told TechCrunch.

On Monday, Corridor said it had raised a $25 million seed round led by Bain Capital Ventures.

Corridor came about after Wagner was in a running accident, and the poor handling of his care led him down a path of “significant, consistent, chronic pain.”

“I developed a long list of complications that needed to be worked through one by one,” he said.

He eventually left Scale AI to get a master’s degree in computer science and electrical engineering at UC Berkeley, before joining Build Robotics in 2023. Later, he teamed up with former Scale AI colleague Eric Qian to work on Capernaum AI, a startup building a clinical agent targeting musculoskeletal care and chronic pain.

The two eventually approached Cold Start to see if they would fund Capernaum, but Aggarwal, who was a partner at Cold Start along with Jason Dong, saw a much larger opportunity. So the four of them took off and launched Corridor together.

“Since health plans are the window through which the vast majority of Americans access health care, it became overwhelmingly clear that one of the highest impact things I could do to improve outcomes for individuals was to create a way for them to access better health plans,” Wagner said.

Other companies in this space include Ignition Benefits and Nava Benefits.

Investors in Corridor’s round include BoxGroup, as well as executives from OpenAI, Scale AI and Ramp. The startup is now preparing for Q4, since “80% of small businesses choose their health plan in Q4,” Aggarwal said.

“Our vision is to build the most trusted healthcare institution in America,” he said. “To earn that, we are laser-focused on a simple promise: doing what we say we’re going to do for the businesses and employees we serve.”

items.summary: Apple is paying $250 million to settle claims that it failed to deliver an AI-upgraded Siri - and now, eligible iPhone owners can submit a claim for a payout. If you live in the US and purchased an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, or any iPhone 16 model between June 10th, 2024,
items.content:
The deadline to file a claim is December 21st, 2026.

Apple is paying $250 million to settle claims that it failed to deliver an AI-upgraded Siri — and now, eligible iPhone owners can submit a claim for a payout. If you live in the US and purchased an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, or any iPhone 16 model between June 10th, 2024, and March 29th, 2025, you can file a claim on the settlement’s website , as reported earlier by MacRumors .

You can receive an estimated $25 per eligible device, but the settlement’s website notes that this can increase to $95 depending on how many people file claims. To file a claim, you’ll need to enter your name, contact information, and iPhone serial number on the settlement’s website before the December 21st, 2026 deadline.

The class action lawsuit alleged Apple created a “clear and reasonable consumer expectation” that new AI features previewed during WWDC 2024 would launch alongside the iPhone 16. Instead, the iPhone 16 launched with a more limited set of capabilities despite being labeled as “built for Apple Intelligence.” The company later delayed the rollout of its AI-upgraded Siri , which only just arrived with iOS 27 earlier this month . Apple has denied any wrongdoing.

items.title: These are the first five Googlebook laptops
items.summary: Google and partners are finally announcing the first laptops under the new Googlebook banner. There are five models from Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo to kick things off. They're available for preorder starting today and arrive in stores on October 4th. Starting prices range f
items.content:
Google’s promising up to 10 years of updates for the new Googlebooks from Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo.

Google and partners are finally announcing the first laptops under the new Googlebook banner. There are five models from Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo to kick things off. They’re available for preorder starting today and arrive in stores on October 4th.

Starting prices range from $899 to $1,299, putting the Googlebooks in the same territory as the MacBook Air and a plethora of Windows laptops. Each Googlebook also comes with 12 months of Google AI Pro with 5TB of cloud storage, along with three-month trials of YouTube Premium, Adobe Photoshop, and CapCut. Google’s also promising up to 10 years of updates.

Here’s a look at the hardware each Googlebook has to offer for those prices, and how they compare to each other.

The Acer Googlebook 14 is the only convertible 2-in-1 in the first round of Googlebooks, featuring a design a bit like Acer’s Chromebook Plus Spin 714. Acer says it offers up to 16 hours of battery life. It also currently has the lowest starting price at $899, although that might not last — Acer’s Kelly Odle said in a comment to The Verge that $899 is the laptop’s “initial launch price available for a limited time,” adding that Acer plans to “reevaluate pricing over time based on component supplies and other market pressures.”

Ongoing shortages of RAM and other components have been driving up prices on other laptops, like Apple’s MacBook Neo , and unfortunately it sounds like a price hike isn’t out of the question for the Acer Googlebook 14, either.

Asus’ Googlebook 14 takes after its ExpertBook Ultra with its design, featuring a metallic gray-blue chassis and more ports than most of the other Googlebooks. It’s the lightest of the first five models at 2.2 pounds, although it isn’t the thinnest (that title goes to Dell). The Asus Googlebook 14 is one of only two that come with an HDMI port as well. It’s one of the pricier Googlebooks, starting at $1,299, but it features spec options similar to the others.

Dell’s first Googlebook, starting at $1,199, closely resembles the XPS 13 but with a light gold “shimmer” colorway, the Googlebook glowbar, and Google’s software. Unlike the Windows XPS 13, the XPS Googlebook also has a fingerprint reader. Unfortunately it’s just as sparse on ports as the original, with only two USB-C ports.

The HP Googlebook 14 starts at $1,299 and notably includes both facial recognition and a fingerprint reader. It also currently has the highest storage capacity on a Googlebook, maxing out at 1TB. It sports a dark blue chassis similar to the HP Spectre, but it’s light on ports with just two USB-C ports and a headphone jack.

Lenovo’s Googlebook starts at the higher end at $1,299, but its 15.3-inch display is the largest display out of the first five models. It’s one of the only ones with an HDMI port, and it’s also the only one with a white chassis, which has a satin-like finish to it, rather than metallic blue or gold. Lenovo’s also launching an AI mouse alongside the Googlebook 15 with a matching glowbar.

items.title: Apple Mac mini review: The new M6 impresses, but the price hike is rough
items.summary: The M4 Mac mini was one of Apple's best values ever. This one, not so much.
items.content:
The new Mac mini is the kind of Mac upgrade Apple has done a million times. It’s the same design as before but with new guts.

These play-it-safe updates aren’t very exciting, but they’re also usually all upside—you get a year or two’s worth of technological improvements for the same price you would have paid for the older version yesterday. Unfortunately, 2026’s unprecedented memory crunch has upended that standard operating procedure.

The new Mac mini starts at $899 for a version with 16GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, a $300 increase for the same memory and storage specs you could get in the $599 M4 Mac mini in 2024.

The M4 Mac mini was a great general-purpose desktop computer and one of the best values Apple had ever offered in a desktop Mac. The M6 Mac mini is only one of those things. I’ll let you guess which.

Note that this review is specifically for the M6 version of the Mac mini. We didn’t get an M5 Pro Mac mini to review, but we’ll talk more about how its pricing and performance fits in for our Mac Studio review.

The M4 Mac minis gave the computers their first full redesigns in nearly 15 years, so it’s not too surprising that the new Mac minis don’t change anything. Compared to the older Intel and M1/M2-era versions, they’re slightly taller (2 inches, up from 1.4), but they have a smaller 5×5-inch footprint (down from 7.7 inches squared). The system is actively cooled, with a fan vent on the bottom to make sure that whatever chip is inside can run at high sustained clock speeds (passively cooled Apple Silicon Macs like the MacBook Air have always been a bit slower than actively cooled Macs with the same chip).

All Mac minis have two 10 Gbps USB-C ports and a headphone jack on the front, and a 2.5 Gbps (default) or 10 Gbps (optional) Ethernet port and HDMI port on the back. Both also have three Thunderbolt ports on the back, but these are Thunderbolt 4 on the M6 Mac mini and Thunderbolt 5 on the M5 Pro version. That means the M6 mini’s ports top out at 40 Gbps, while the M5 Pro mini supports up to 120 Gbps speeds.

Realistically, there aren’t a ton of things on a Mac that can use all that bandwidth, especially since Apple doesn’t support external GPUs. But you do need a Thunderbolt 5 Mac to daisy-chain multiple computers together to form a compute cluster, so if that’s something you’re interested in, keep it in mind when you buy—maybe you’re buying multiple desktops, or maybe you already have an M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pro you’d like to test the feature with.

The only real gripe with this design continues to be its bottom-rear-mounted power button; apparently, complaints about this are being sent to the same trash can Apple has always used for complaints about the Magic Mouse’s bottom-mounted charging port. It doesn’t come up often in everyday use if you just let your Mac go to sleep rather than shutting it down. But the positioning problem does really call attention to itself when you pair a TouchID-equipped external keyboard with the mini, since it requires a quick double-tap of the Mac’s power button before the sensor will work.

Apple’s first M6-series chip is making its debut in the humble Mac mini, and the chip looks like the biggest upgrade Apple’s lower-end chip has gotten since the M4 generation added extra efficiency cores.

The headliner is the presence of two of Apple’s so-called “Super” cores , Apple’s nomenclature for P-cores that are even faster than its typical P-cores. Those are added on top of four P-cores and six E-cores for a total of 12 CPU cores. M4 and M5 both had 10 CPU cores. In the M4, these were split between four regular P-cores and six E-cores, whereas the M5 split them between four super cores and six E-cores (the M5’s cores were referred to as P-cores when it launched but were rebranded later when the M5 Pro and Max came out). The M1, M2, and M3 generations all used four P-cores and four E-cores.

The M6 has fewer super cores than the M5 but the same number of E-cores and four additional P-cores. While they’re apparently no longer “super,” the P-cores still perform well enough to ensure that the M6’s multi-core performance is better than M5’s overall.

Apple has mixed super cores with both other kinds of cores before, but this is its first chip to include all three kinds at once. To get around the awkwardness this might create at the CPU scheduler level, the built-in powermetrics tool suggests that Apple is still treating the M6 like a chip with just two types of cores. The six E-cores are all gathered together in one cluster, and the two Super cores and the four P-cores are all lumped together into a second six-core cluster called the “PS cluster.”

Powermetrics also reports that both the P- and S-cores have the same peak and minimum clock speeds, unlike in the M5 Pro and M5 Max where they’re different clusters with different clock speeds (both P- and S-cores in M6 range from 1.44 GHz to 4.79 GHz). The sysctl utility also suggests they share the same 20MB pool of L2 cache, up from 16MB for the 4-core Super cluster in the M5 (the E-core cluster has a bit more L2 cache, too, 8MB up from 6MB in the M5). The Super cores do have more L1 instruction and data cache, so they are definitely still different cores, and there are likely other differences that we can’t detect using software-level tools. But if you were wondering how macOS was going to treat a chip with three different kinds of CPU cores at a software level, the answer is “to act like it still has two different kinds of cores.”

items.title: Googlebooks launch October 4 starting at $899—here are the five models you can preorder today
items.summary: Googlebooks offer premium hardware and deep smartphone integration, but you may not like the price.
items.content:
Google is ready to take a swing at laptops… again. The company has had a lot of success in phones, but it has struggled to parlay that into an effective strategy for larger screens. Chromebooks have been fine as a budget option, but it seems like Google has accepted they’ll never compete with macOS or Windows. That’s where Googlebooks come in. These new Android-powered laptops are intended to be “real” computers, featuring premium hardware, on-device apps, and powerful development tools.

After the Googlebook reveal at I/O this year , Google’s partners are now ready to sell you one. The first Googlebooks are available from several OEMs that have been making Chromebooks over the years, but don’t expect Chromebook pricing. There’s only one model under a grand, and the rest are well above that.

The bulk of Chromebooks have been budget machines, and they looked the part. Googlebooks, however, feature bright OLED screens, metal builds, big haptic trackpads, and the Glowbar. All the machines have this illuminated bar on the lid, but it doesn’t do much for now. It lights up when the device boots and can display battery level, but Google says it’s going to release an API for developers to add more features.

Across the full lineup, Google says you can expect 16GB of RAM with 32GB upgrades for some models. At launch, the machines will run either a Snapdragon X Elite or an Intel Core Ultra Series 3 (Panther Lake) chip. Both platforms have an NPU capable of 45 TOPS of on-device AI performance, and all the designs are fanless. Regardless of the exact model, Google says you can expect up to 14 hours of video playback and 16 hours of web browsing.

Here are all the launch models and their starting prices.

The Acer model is the cheapest, and it’s also the only convertible in the lineup. The price jump from that device to the next cheapest (the Dell XPS) is a substantial $300, and the rest of the launch laptops are $100 more than that. Google’s partners launched a few Chromebooks in this price range, but they didn’t see wide adoption.

A major part of Chrome’s failure to truly compete with macOS and Windows is down to software availability. Google tried multiple ways to shoehorn local apps into its web-first platform, but it never took. The advantage of starting from scratch, according to Google, is that these new laptops share the same software stack as Android phones. That means you can run Android apps natively without all the VM weirdness of ChromeOS, and there are a ton of those.

Google is aware of the sordid history of running phone apps on desktop PCs. It’s often a clunky experience using a phone app designed for touch on a large screen with a keyboard and mouse, but the company claims you may be surprised how many apps in the Play Store are now optimized for laptops. The Play Store client will call out apps and games that have been optimized for bigger displays, and Google says more apps are being updated for laptops all the time. There will also be a “desktop-class” version of the Chrome browser preinstalled on Googlebooks.

Even if optimized, these are still going to be apps designed for, and primarily used on, smartphones. It’s unclear if they’ll offer the kind of power people expect for a $1,300 laptop. On the gaming side, Google notes that its Level Up program is delivering more experiences suitable for a keyboard and mouse, but the selection of desktop-ready games won’t be anything like what you get on Windows or macOS.

There is, of course, nothing stopping you from using phone apps on a Googlebook if you want. They’ll run in a window, and you may not even need to install them. With Cast My Apps, the apps installed on your Android phone are available instantly on a Googlebook. They appear in a dedicated app list on the laptop, allowing you to open and use them without touching the phone. The file manager can also seamlessly access files on your Android phone.

Similarly, a feature called Continue On lets you pick up where you were in a phone app on the Googlebook version of the app. This requires developer support, so not all apps will carry over. Still, this level of integration with Android is not something you get on either Windows or macOS, which could make a Googlebook appealing if you’ve got a Pixel or Galaxy riding around in your pocket.

As you would expect, the Play Store is the primary source of apps for Googlebooks, and there will be some limits on sideloading. Google has confirmed to Ars that Googlebooks will enforce developer verification requirements for apps similar to Android phones. Under this system, only apps from developers who have verified their identities with Google will be eligible for installation from a downloaded APK file. This requirement will roll out broadly next year, but it’s being activated in a few markets in the coming weeks .

Google is following through on its promise to make AI a core part of the Googlebook experience. Gemini models are going to be deeply integrated with the software, ready to work on your screen context with a cursor wiggle. Google calls this Magic Pointer, and it has a few suggestions about how to use it.

Let’s say you have an email or PDF with dates you need to add to your calendar. You can jiggle the cursor, point Gemini at the email, and get all the dates added in one go. If you get a suspicious email, you can invoke Gemini with your cursor and ask it to figure out if it’s a scam. You can also point Gemini at images and tell it to edit them or generate new versions without downloading anything. Useful? Maybe occasionally, but Google’s enthusiasm for Magic Pointer seems a bit premature.

이번 협력은 스냅드래곤 X 엘리트의 전력 효율과 연산 성능, 강력한 온디바이스 AI 처리 역량을 구글의 제미나이 인텔리전스와 기기 수준에서 결합해 사용자에게 선제적이고 고도화된 맞춤형 컴퓨팅 환경을 제공하기 위해 추진됐다.

구글북은 모바일과 PC를 아우르는 심리스(Seamless·끊김 없는) 연결성을 특징으로 한다. 스냅드래곤 기반의 안드로이드 스마트폰 및 태블릿과 유기적인 ‘크로스 디바이스(Cross-device)’ 연동을 지원하며, 수천 개에 달하는 네이티브 안드로이드 애플리케이션(앱)과 게임을 PC 환경에서 직접 구동할 수 있도록 구축됐다.

이를 지원하기 위한 핵심 생산성 기능도 대거 탑재된다. ▲캐스트 마이 앱스(Cast my Apps) ▲매직 포인터(Magic Pointer) ▲램블러(Rambler) 등의 기능이 적용돼 이메일, 캘린더 일정, 디스플레이에 표시된 콘텐츠 등에서 필요한 맥락을 AI가 파악해 실시간으로 정보를 제공한다. 또한 스마트폰과의 매끄러운 연동과 온디바이스 기반의 첨단 보안성을 확보해 작업의 연속성과 생산성을 끌어올렸다.

게이밍과 엔터테인먼트 성능도 놓치지 않았다. 글로벌 안드로이드 앱 생태계를 기반으로 콘텐츠 제작과 학습, 게임 플레이를 지원하며, 더 빠른 프레임 속도와 그래픽 렌더링 품질을 제공하는 ‘스냅드래곤 엘리트 게이밍’의 핵심 기술도 함께 적용됐다.

케다르 콘답(Kedar Kondap) 퀄컴 수석 부사장 겸 컴퓨트·게이밍 본부장은 “스냅드래곤 X 엘리트의 선도적인 AI 역량은 퍼스널 컴퓨팅 경험을 혁신하며 더욱 지능적이고 개인화된 생산성 경험을 위한 새로운 가능성을 열었다”며 “뛰어난 성능과 효율성을 바탕으로 구글북 사용자에게 네이티브 안드로이드 앱과 게임까지 지원하게 됐다”고 설명했다.

이어 “퀄컴과 구글은 글로벌 OEM들과 긴밀히 협력해 스냅드래곤 기반의 새로운 노트북 카테고리가 선사하는 최첨단 기능을 구현하고, 스냅드래곤 안드로이드 스마트폰 사용자들에게 기기 간 경계가 없는 경험을 제공할 것”이라고 덧붙였다.

items.title: The long dream of the Googlebook
items.summary: In late 2010, an up-and-coming Google executive named Sundar Pichai took the stage in front of a bunch of reporters and explained that Google had a big new idea about laptops. In the future, he said, the only thing you'd need on your computer was a web browser - that was where al
items.content:
Google’s latest attempt to reinvent the laptop will require everything the company does well — and a few things it doesn’t.

Photography by Antonio G. Di Benedetto

In late 2010, an up-and-coming Google executive named Sundar Pichai took the stage in front of a bunch of reporters and explained that Google had a big new idea about laptops. In the future, he said, the only thing you’d need on your computer was a web browser — that was where all your apps, data, and connections would live going forward. Your computer didn’t need much storage, Pichai explained, or any fancy hardware, because the cloud would do the work. The software designed for these new laptops, Chrome OS , was an enormous bet that the web would eventually overtake everything.

Chrome OS (which eventually became ChromeOS ) has been, in many ways, a huge hit. But the computer currently on Rick Osterloh’s desk isn’t a Chromebook. Osterloh is Google’s head of hardware and devices, and the sleek, slim device he’s tapping on as he joins our Google Meet is a 13-inch Dell clamshell with decidedly un-Chromebook specs: 16 gigs of RAM, a cutting-edge Qualcomm processor, a light and thin and MacBook-ish metallic look. It’s called the XPS Googlebook, and it’s one of five new devices running Googlebook OS, Google’s latest big idea about computers.

At first blush, Googlebooks feel like classic Google in a bad way: yet another operating system, yet another brand, yet another thing destined for the Google graveyard. But Osterloh sees it differently. He greenlit the whole project in part because he saw it as “the ultimate focusing move” for Google. For a long time, he says, Google has built, maintained, and shipped two operating systems. ChromeOS stayed on laptops, while Android conquered phones and tablets and TVs and cars and everything else. Slowly but surely, Google has built Android into a familiar interface and a large app ecosystem across all those devices. Except for laptops.

Meanwhile, Google became convinced that the advent of AI might change the way we use computers forever — but might not need to change the computers themselves. Osterloh says he has tables full of wheel-reinventing prototypes, and of course the company is betting big on things like smart glasses, but high-end PCs, which have the power needed to run AI models for coding, dictation, and more, have been a surprise winner of the AI revolution so far. (Just ask Apple, which has seen AI enthusiasts buy high-end Macs in huge volume.) “I think laptops are one of those resonant form factors,” Osterloh says. “It’s an established category that’s incredibly useful for productivity and apps, and it’s going to be really hard to replace that.”

Those two ideas together — Android’s dominance and the rise of AI — tell the whole story of Googlebook. There are a lot of bets inside of the Googlebook project, both about what we do on computers and how we’ll do it going forward, but maybe the most surprising is Google’s commitment to building kickass laptops. A generation ago, then-CEO Eric Schmidt argued that the future was “ disposable ” hardware, that devices wouldn’t matter as the internet took over. Googlebooks represent Google’s growing belief that devices matter more than ever. And that a good laptop is worth paying for.

“The key thing that had changed was just the rapid pace of evolution that Android itself has gone under.”

The Googlebook project started in earnest a couple of years ago, but some of the ideas have been floating around much longer . Rumors and reports of a ChromeOS-Android merger have been around for more than a decade , and Google has tried various ways to bring the two operating systems into harmony. The company spent years programming ChromeOS to be able to run Android apps (and even Windows apps ), but never nailed the integration. For years, a project called Fuchsia looked like the combination users had been waiting for, but that petered out into a smart home-specific project.

In early 2024, though, a couple of Googlers asked a new question: What if, instead of trying to bring Android apps to ChromeOS, we brought the best of ChromeOS to Android? They weren’t the first people to ask that question, but they were the first to time it right. “The key thing that had changed,” says Prajakta Gudadhe, Google’s VP of engineering for laptops and tablets, “was just the rapid pace of evolution that Android itself has gone under.”

For so many years, Android was a phone operating system that was sometimes hamfistedly shoved into other devices. But Gudadhe felt like Android had finally matured into something truly cross-platform. Developers had begun to embrace multiple screen sizes and orientations, and the Android team at Google had changed the way they built the operating system. “Android at that time was serving multiple form factors, from phones to wearables to TVs to autos,” Gudadhe says, “and because of that they just had to invest in a much more modular stack that could support this diversity.”

What that meant in practice was that it might finally be possible to build an Android laptop that could natively run the universe of Android apps, without looking and working like a grossly oversized Android phone. By combining base Android technology with some of the best features of ChromeOS — excellent multitasking and multi-window support, fast boot times, easy software updates — Google could have the best of both worlds.

The idea became a memo proposing a new laptop OS, which was excitedly received by Google leadership, and Project Aluminium was born. (To be clear: It is A-lu-min-i-um, not aluminum, and there was a swear jar in the office for people who dared to pronounce it the American way.)

items.title: I got to see Google’s wild ideas about the future of laptops
items.summary: There are a few things about using a Googlebook that immediately feel just right. The hardware is polished (since it's based on current laptops). The OS is familiar (if you've ever used a Chromebook). But most impressive, it integrates your Android phone with your PC so they feel
items.content:
﻿Googlebooks are here. And they’re actually interesting (for Android phone users) — but there are still so many questions.

There are a few things about using a Googlebook that immediately feel just right. The hardware is polished (since it’s based on current laptops). The OS is familiar (if you’ve ever used a Chromebook). But most impressive, it integrates your Android phone with your PC so they feel more like one device. It’s the culmination of a series of new ideas that blur the two devices together. After my first look, I went from doubtful to excited by the prospect of Google pulling it all off.

After an initial barebones announcement in May, Google is finally launching Googlebooks — its new line of Android-based laptops. The initial five Googlebook models from Dell, Lenovo, HP, Acer, and Asus all launch October 4th, with preorders available now and starting prices ranging from $899 to $1,299.

So what are Googlebooks?

In a nutshell, they’re laptops running a new operating system that’s a blend of Chromebooks and Android — with a whole lot of Gemini AI stuff built in. They look quite like Chromebooks, but with Android’s Material Three Expressive UI stylings on the software side and higher-end materials for hardware. There doesn’t seem to be a baseline spec for Googlebooks, but at launch they’re all thin-and-light laptops ranging from 13 inches to 15 inches with 16GB of RAM or more, touchscreen displays (most of them OLED), metal chassis, backlit keyboards, either fingerprint or facial recognition unlocking (or both), and a Google-y Glowbar light strip on their lids.

Powering the initial lineup of Googlebooks are Intel Core Ultra Series 3 “Panther Lake” and Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite chips, with MediaTek options expected to come later. While the first wave of Googlebooks are similarly sized and all have “Googlebook” in their name, there are some variations: haptic or mechanical trackpads, port offerings, even a 2-in-1 convertible. Check out our roundup of all the hardware here .

I spent a bit of time prodding all the Googlebooks during my demos, and each one felt pretty nice. They each have their own unique qualities: the Asus was incredibly lightweight, the Lenovo has plenty of ports and an optional mouse with a matching Glowbar light, the Acer’s convertible form factor allows some tablet-like use (and it’s pretty affordable for a Panther Lake laptop). The HP had a great looking screen and a latticeless keyboard I surprisingly didn’t hate, and the Dell is basically a gold XPS 13 ( which is excellent ) but with a different chip.

But everything really special about Googlebooks comes down to software. They run Googlebook OS, which is built with the native Android stack atop a Linux kernel and supports both x86 and Arm architectures (as implied by the chip offerings). It’s an Android desktop interface that runs Android apps and feels much like ChromeOS, but it’s got some handy features when paired with an Android phone.

You can cast apps from an Android phone directly to a Googlebook, even without touching your phone. Googlebooks essentially have two app drawers: a G-logo start menu for installed Googlebook apps and a second one beside it that pulls up mobile apps from your phone. Click a phone app and you can fully use that app with the mouse and keyboard or the Googlebook’s touchscreen. It’s a bit like iPhone Mirroring on macOS, but the apps are individually extracted to the desktop OS instead of showing your whole phone interface.

Googlebooks also have a nifty feature called Continue On where the icons of apps you’re currently using on your phone appear in the bottom bar — allowing you to click it on the laptop and hand it off to the Googlebook. These app handoffs can transition to a native app or a web app, depending on how developers have programmed it. A Google rep informed me at my in-person briefing that Continue On is fairly simple for Android developers to add to their apps, and casting apps to a Googlebook doesn’t require anything extra.

The other big way Googlebooks interact with an Android phone is Quick Access, allowing you to see and access all the files stored on your phone right in the desktop Files app. The paired Android phone is listed in the sidebar of a Googlebook’s Files window, just like any other drive or home folder, and you can directly search it and share files from it without physically picking up your phone. This is pretty handy stuff, but of course it all requires you running an Android phone. If you have an iPhone then you’re limited to a Link to iOS app that just does some message syncing and replying.

As Google first showed back in May, the Googlebook mouse cursor is called a Magic Pointer — allowing you to wiggle it to summon Gemini. Doing so allows you to ask Gemini questions or have it look at things on your screen to get further info. One of Google’s live demos was asking Gemini “Is this legit?” on a Spotify account authentication email, or adding a multi-week exercise routine for marathon training to a Google Calendar. Some tasks run locally, while many will go up to Gemini in the cloud — and it wasn’t clear when that was happening during any of Google’s demos. Googlebooks also have recent Android features like Create My Widget (for creating custom widgets from natural language prompts) and Rambler (speech transcription that can parse stream of consciousness-like wordiness).

items.title: The M5 Ultra Mac Studio tears through our benchmark tests
items.summary: The Mac Studio review unit that Apple sent us to test this year is, put simply, kind of outrageous. It has an M5 Ultra chip with a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU, 256GB of RAM, and 4TB of storage and costs $12,299. This thing is not for your typical content creation workloads. It's
items.content:
﻿There’s a lot to consider with Apple’s over-the-top $12,300 computer, so this is just a first taste.

Photography by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge

The Mac Studio review unit that Apple sent us to test this year is, put simply, kind of outrageous. It has an M5 Ultra chip with a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU, 256GB of RAM, and 4TB of storage and costs $12,299. This thing is not for your typical content creation workloads. It’s for AI developers and some of the most demanding 3D visual effects houses out there.

Frankly, our usual benchmarks aren’t cutting it.

The latest version of Apple’s most powerful computer begins shipping today with new chips and prices that extend even further into the stratosphere. The new Mac Studio uses the same design that’s been with us since 2022 , replete with ultra-fast ports both front and back, now kitted out with either an M5 Max or M5 Ultra chip, compared to the M4 Max or M3 Ultra of last year’s model .

The M5 Max model starts at a relatively modest $2,499 with an 18-core CPU / 32-core GPU, 36GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage. We’ve tested an M5 Max already, in the MacBook Pro , where it starts at $4,099 with the same amount of memory and 2TB of storage (the equivalent Mac Studio costs $3,299). The M5 Ultra is another beast altogether. It starts at $5,499 with 30 CPU cores, 64 GPU cores, 96GB of memory and 1TB of storage.

I’ve only had my hands on the new Mac Studio as well as a pair of the latest Mac Minis for a handful of days. That’s enough time to adequately test the M6 and M5 Pro chips in the Mac Mini , and to run our standard benchmarks on the M5 Ultra — but not enough time to seriously challenge it.

Conveniently, we still have the similarly specced M3 Ultra Mac Studio from last year — though it was only $8,099 at the time. Aside from CPU core count and architecture, they’re nearly the same, which makes them easy to compare.

The M5 Ultra Mac Studio is around 30 percent faster than our similarly configured M3 Ultra in both single-core and multicore synthetic CPU tests. It varies more in graphics tests, but some, like the new Geekbench 7 OpenCL test, also saw around a 30 percent uplift. And a heftier GPU rendering test like Cinebench scored 63 percent higher.

I’ve never tested anything this fast before. The storage speeds are off the proverbial charts. It renders the classroom test in Blender faster than I can tie my shoes. Our Premiere 4K video export test, which yields an MP4 file of about 1.7GB, is done in about 40 seconds. I can’t get up from my desk and get a cup of coffee that fast without risking a serious burn.

Apple is talking a big game about the M5 Ultra being “a monumental step for AI.” I don’t normally run local AI stuff (I just don’t find generative AI and LLM stuff very useful for my work — and I’ve tried ). But I want to give it a serious go, so I’m open to suggestions. I’ve already reached out to our great Verge audience for ideas , and I appreciate all of you who commented. (Yes, even those of you with the “Can it run DOOM ” jokes. I see you, and it never gets old. I mean, it does. But it doesn’t. I love DOOM .)

How long is this going to take me? Hopefully not very long, but it’s going to be a busy couple of months. Google is announcing its whole new line of Googlebook laptops at exactly the same time this article publishes. And there’s a Microsoft event coming up next week that sounds a whole lot like it’ll jumpstart Nvidia’s RTX Spark initiative . There’s never a drought of laptops to test, but this Techtember and Techtober seems like a deluge that’s about to engulf Your Friendly Neighborhood Laptop Reviewer.

I know, I know; “So many cool computers to test, what a burden.” Truly, it is a very exciting time for computers. An expensive one, for sure , but I don’t think the space has ever been this dynamic. So I’ll do my best to get back to you when I’ve got something cool to share about the M5 Ultra Mac Studio. Feel free to drop more ideas and tips in the comments here. Or email me or DM me on Bluesky if you’ve got suggestions you’d like to share. I also accept words of encouragement and compliments. :)

The M5 Ultra Mac Studio is a powerful machine. Let’s see if we can find its limits. Stay tuned.

items.title: Googlebooks feel like the first laptops built for Android owners
items.summary: There's a good chance that my next laptop will be a Googlebook. If you're an Android user like me, then yours might be too, because Google is making a compelling pitch: The Googlebook does for the Android phone what the MacBook does for the iPhone (and then some). John Maletis, G
items.content:
App casting, handoff, and seamless file sharing make Googlebooks feel (almost) obvious with an Android phone.

There’s a good chance that my next laptop will be a Googlebook. If you’re an Android user like me, then yours might be too, because Google is making a compelling pitch: The Googlebook does for the Android phone what the MacBook does for the iPhone (and then some).

John Maletis, Google’s head of laptops and tablets, said at my press briefing that the Googlebooks were designed to “work seamlessly with your Android phone.” You can start using an app on your phone then pick it up on the laptop, navigate your phone’s files from the laptop, run any phone app from the computer, and manage all your notifications in one place.

It’s a good pitch. And after spending a couple of hours playing with the first five Googlebooks — from Lenovo, Dell, HP, Acer, and Asus — I really hope Google delivers on it.

The enhanced integration begins at setup, which lets you link your Google account and Android device so that the laptop syncs your contacts, passwords, preferred settings, payment details, and more, just like it would when you switch from one Android phone to another.

Googlebook OS is built on Android’s codebase, but its interface is a blend of Android and ChromeOS. The layout mostly feels like a Chromebook, but the details of the UI are drawn from Android, specifically the Material 3 Expressive design language found primarily across Google’s own Pixel phones. Everything from widget design to the notification tray looks and feels like Android, only blown up a little to fill the space.

Connect a Googlebook to your phone and each is supposed to feel like an extension of the other. Notifications are shared, and dismissing or reading them on one device will carry through to the other. You can also use the laptop to send in-line replies to messages sent to your phone.

File sharing is intended to be just as simple. The Googlebook file browser lists a paired phone among the hard drives, letting you go straight in to browse, open, edit, and copy files. No more uploading and downloading files with Google Drive or sending them as email attachments just to move them to the laptop.

There’s a version of Continue On , an Android 17 feature first introduced for tablets this year. It allows you to start using an app on your phone and pick it up on your laptop, though only certain apps are compatible. You can also open any phone app directly from the laptop via a dedicated app drawer. Apps are run on the phone itself, and simply cast to the laptop, where they’re displayed in a floating portrait window — though you can’t mirror the full phone itself, only individual apps. It’s less flexible, but also less fiddly.

The most exciting features here — Continue On, app casting, file browsing — all require a phone running Android 17 . For the moment that’s most Pixels and a handful of flagships from Samsung and other manufacturers, so Android’s fragmented updates will throttle immediate demand for Googlebooks. Future features may require more advanced Android versions of course, but Google says this core set should keep working even if your phone software gets a little behind. That’s reassuring, since the laptops will likely outlast your phone, with Google promising 10 years of software support.

Much of this isn’t new to Googlebooks. ChromeOS has been steadily adding integrations with Android over the years, and these new laptops build on that work. Chromebooks have been able to sync notifications, share passwords and payment cards, and even stream or emulate Android apps. Even Windows delivers its own version of these features via Phone Link , with notification syncing, screen mirroring, and a basic version of handoff. Googlebooks make these features quicker and simpler to access, and make sure that they work across every Android 17 phone, rather than Pixels and a handful more. Making an Android phone work with a Chromebook or Windows laptop has always taken a little effort; making it work with a Googlebook should require almost none.

Shifting Googlebook OS to Android’s tech stack means it can run Android apps without any emulation, and gets full access to the Play Store. If you can run an app on your phone, you can run it on your Googlebook. Google has worked with major players to ensure support already, including streamers Netflix, Disney Plus, and HBO Max — and because these are technically still mobile apps, you can download series and films to watch offline, unlike on most other laptops.

One worry is that all of this might get a little confusing. Some apps will run in small, phone-shaped windows with a vertical UI, some will scale dynamically for the big screen, and others will have dedicated desktop versions optimized for a laptop layout. Some of those desktop-optimized apps can be shrunk down to a phone UI if you prefer, some can’t. Sometimes apps will run natively on the laptop hardware, other times you’ll cast them from your phone. Some apps will support Continue On’s handoff between devices, most (at least at launch) won’t — though a Google rep told me it’s “a couple lines” of code to add support, and so they’re optimistic about uptake.

Google is trying to manage the possible confusion with new Play Store tags that let you know if an app is designed or optimized for desktop, or whether you’re better off using the web version instead. The app store homepage will also default to promoting apps that should run well on a laptop, so phone-first apps will only show up when you search for them.

items.title: Got an Android Phone? Google Thinks You’ll Probably Want a Googlebook Laptop
items.summary: Apple lovers have long enjoyed seamless connectivity between their iPhones and Macs. Now, Google’s bringing that experience to Android.
items.content:
iPhones and Macs are like two peas in a pod. Apple’s hardware synergy means you can launch iPhone apps right from the macOS desktop , respond to texts without picking up your iPhone, and even copy text on one platform and paste it on the other. That kind of seamless connectivity does not natively exist for Android phone owners at the operating system level.

Google’s trying to change that with Googlebooks , a new class of laptop. First teased in May , the company finally shared more details about the new OS at a media-only event in New York City last week. Like with Android , hardware manufacturers can make their own Googlebooks, provided they hit specific standards set by Google.

Preorders open today, and the machines hit store shelves on October 4, starting at $899. Every purchase includes a full year of Google AI Pro service with 5 terabytes of storage.

Here are the new laptops, all of which are clamshells except the Acer, which is a 2-in-1 machine :

Some of the standards Google has set include using “premium materials,” like aluminum, magnesium, or carbon fiber, to make them lightweight. They need at least 16 GB of RAM, deliver more than 45 tera operations per second (TOPS) , a touchscreen (LCD or OLED), a backlit keyboard, a haptic trackpad, Dolby Atmos speakers, studio-quality microphones with noise cancellation, and at least 14 hours of battery life. Googlebooks will receive 10 years of software updates.

They must feature the Glowbar—the signature LED strip on the laptop’s exterior that identifies the machine as a Googlebook. It’s a callback to the glowbar Google used on its original Chromebook Pixel . (Speaking of which, Google hasn’t shared whether it’s making its own Googlebook under its Made by Google Pixel hardware division.) Developers can access the Glowbar to customize the lights to specific actions in their apps, and there’s also an Easter egg app consumers can unlock to customize the light color and animation themselves. Like HiLight introduced on the latest Pixel phones , the Glowbar will illuminate when you talk to Gemini.

Googlebooks have a slightly custom keyboard with a G key for Gemini, and the Caps key doubles as the Quick Insert key.

“There’s a lot the laptop gets right, but much of it was designed decades ago, before mobile devices were invented,” Sameer Samat, president of the Android ecosystem, said at the event. “Reinventing laptops is a multi-year endeavor. Our first step is to focus on the Android community because today there isn’t a laptop that is designed to seamlessly work with your Android phone.”

Googlebook merges Android’s mobile-first operating system with ChromeOS, the OS powering Chromebooks . Google says Chromebooks aren’t going anywhere and will continue to serve schools and act as the budget-friendly option for consumers. While the Googlebook interface feels like a blown-up version of Android, it’s not just an Android-powered desktop. Rather, it’s a distinct OS optimized for x86 and ARM chip architectures.

What’s particularly interesting is how Android apps work on the device. They’re categorized in three ways. When you set up your Googlebook with your Android phone, important data flows seamlessly to the laptop, including Wi-Fi networks, passwords, settings, messages, contacts, and photos. Not all of your phone apps will automatically be installed, though, as Google deems some apps as “better on the web," like Facebook. (You can still install the Facebook app if you want and get the mobile-shaped experience.)

There are three ratings for apps on the Google Play Store: Made for Desktop, Optimized for Desktop, and Better on the Website.

The next tier of Android app is “Optimized for Desktop.” These apps take advantage of the bigger screens with better layouts and a little more functionality. The final tier is “Made for Desktop,” like the desktop versions of Chrome. Google says around 20 or so apps are either optimized for desktop or made for the desktop so far, including CapCut, Adobe Photoshop, Notability, and Fantastical . As the platform grows, Google expects more developers will target Android’s “Made for Desktop” tier and bring their desktop-grade apps from Windows and macOS to Googlebook.

People want to play games on their laptops, and so Google says you’ll be able to access more than 20,000 titles on the Play Store, many of which support cross-device play between mobile, tablets, and laptops. Google says around 50 of the 100 top titles are optimized for keyboard, trackpad, and touchscreen. But since you can’t download AAA games for Googlebooks (yet), especially without a discrete GPU , Google is offering 1 year of Nvidia’s GeForce Now game streaming service, which is optimized for the platform.

Googlebook is an opportunity for Google to bring artificial intelligence to the forefront of the laptop computing experience, which is why many of the core new features are AI-powered. For example, similar to Android 17 , you can generate your own desktop widgets with simple prompts to Gemini.

Magic Pointer is the marquee Gemini feature. Wiggle the mouse pointer over anything, and a Gemini overlay will suggest contextual actions. For example, if you wiggle over an event someone invited you to, you’ll get a prompt to automatically “Create an event” and have it added to your Google Calendar with one tap. Or if you’re wondering what breed of dog you’re looking at (whether it’s a video or photo), wiggle and ask Gemini, “What’s the breed?” If you’re wondering whether an email is a phishing attempt, wiggle over it and ask Gemini.

Wiggle your cursor anywhere, and the Magic Pointer will do its thing and understand the context of the area you select.

items.title: Apple Mac Mini (M6) Review: For the AI Curious
items.summary: Apple has refreshed the Mac Mini with a brand-new chip, the M6. And this time, it’s more focused on AI than ever.
items.content:
The Mac Mini has gone through a Peter Parker-esque transformation this year. Just six months ago, it was a meek, unassuming little Mac starter kit, content to fulfill the role of being Apple's smallest and most affordable Mac. It was so easy to overlook that Apple even skipped its M5 refresh last year.

But at the beginning of 2026, the world was flooded with agentic AI frameworks like Claude Cowork, OpenClaw , and Perplexity Computer. Suddenly, the Mac Mini became a hot commodity for running AI models. Before long, it was completely sold out and hard to find for most of the year. Even Apple was caught off guard .

The M6 Mac Mini isn't designed to be flashy. It's meant to blend into your desk's workspace, maybe even hidden behind your monitor or in a closet. That's not necessarily because it's ugly or poorly made, though. The chassis was redesigned for the 2024 M4 release , adopting a boxier look and overall smaller form factor. It fits in your hand, with a footprint of just 5 x 5 inches. It's tiny and well crafted. Everything is inside, including the power supply—no huge power brick to have to find a spot for.

Ports remain the same. Two forward-facing USB-C 3 ports (up to 10 gigabytes per second), as well as a headphone jack and a power indicator light. On the back, there are three Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1, an Ethernet jack, and the power adapter port. Using the available USB-C ports and HDMI on the back, you can connect up to two 5K 120-Hz external displays (such as the Studio Display XDR or BenQ 5K MA270S) or three 4K displays.

One controversial design is that the power button is still hidden underneath the back left corner of the computer. If you know where it is, just tilt the Mac Mini to the side and reach your finger back—easy. If you don't know (or keep forgetting, as I do), it means having to flip the thing over entirely, with all your cables attached. It remains a silly design decision in my view, but it's nowhere near as egregious as the Magic Mouse it pairs with (sold separately), which still infamously charges from the bottom. But I digress.

I still wish it had an SD card slot (forward-facing, like the Mac Studio ) though. Plenty of photographers and videographers would be well suited for the Mac Mini, and yet they'll need to buy an additional dock or adapter. And yes, some color options, like the iMac, would be nice. But from the outside, it's the same well-built, compact mini PC it's always been. It's the performance under the hood where you'll need to dig in to see the extra value in this latest generation.

Right off the bat, I was eager to test a couple of new components in the M6 Mac Mini. First, there are the advances in the M6 chip itself. This is our first glimpse of the next generation of Apple Silicon, and the first built on a 2-nm process node. It represents a significant step up in transistor count on the die—46 billion in this case. That's around a 35 percent increase in transistor density, which translates to higher efficiency and more performance. In theory.

The M6 Mac Mini also adds two more CPU cores than the M4 model, for a total of 12. That's a 21 percent increase in single-thread performance and a 36 percent improvement in a multi-threaded run. Those numbers sound impressive, but compared to the M5 in the MacBook Air , they're not as substantial. It's only around 10 percent faster than the M5 Pro chip in the MacBook Pro in single-threaded performance (and unsurprisingly, much further behind in multi-threaded). Those two extra CPU cores, though, do prop up the multi-threaded performance, even compared to the base M5 chip. It's hard to do apples-to-apples comparisons to only a laptop.

Like previous Mac Minis, it has a fan inside. And when you get to work on something heavy, you'll definitely hear it start to make some noise. It's not terrible, but if you're coming from a MacBook, you'll definitely notice. That active cooling ensures you get stronger performance from that M6 chip than you would in a MacBook Air (though I won't be able to do a side-by-side comparison until the M6 MacBook Air comes out, presumably in 2027).

Apple skipped the M5 generation for the Mac Mini, so this is the first time the Mac Mini gets the Neural Accelerators built into each GPU core. That means improved local AI inferencing, which brings me to the second thing I really wanted to try out. Despite the base model only having 16 GB of RAM, it took an average of 1 minute and 40 seconds to generate a 20-step image in Draw Things using the Flux.2 model on the M6 Mac Mini. This is a 9-billion-parameter AI model being run completely locally, without going to the cloud. My 16-inch M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 48 GB of RAM was faster, however, generating this same image 20 seconds faster. Still, I was really impressed by the M6, and I chalk it up to the beefed-up GPU.

The M6 chip also includes a “dual” Neural Engine. Apple hasn't talked extensively about how exactly this works, but claims that it delivers twice the “peak compute” to speed up on-device AI workflows and that these frameworks can automatically access and use both Neural Engines at the same time. This will enhance all kinds of in-app features that creatives may appreciate, such as detecting edits in raw footage in Final Cut Pro. This can be done relatively seamlessly. It doesn't necessarily apply to running models on-device as a replacement for ChatGPT or Gemini. I tested out the same 70-billion-parameter Llama 2 model in LM Studio that I tested on previous Macs, but the application couldn't load it, saying it required 32 GB of memory to run well. I tried to load it anyway, which did, indeed, cause my system to freeze immediately.

미국 워싱턴주 벨뷰(Bellevue)에 본사가 있는 글로벌 보안기업 태니엄(한국지사장 박영선)이 앤트로픽(Anthropic)의 '프로젝트 글래스윙(Project Glasswing)'에 참여한다. 자사 방어적 사이버보안 업무에 클로드 미토스 5(Claude Mythos 5)를 테스트하고 있다고 21일 발표했다.

태니엄은 이 모델을 자사의 프로덕션 코드베이스, 즉 전 세계 수천 개 기업의 IT 및 보안 운영자가 엔드포인트 자산을 관리하고 보호하는 데 사용하는 소프트웨어에 직접 적용하고 있다. 태니엄은 이번 프로젝트를 통해 얻은 결과를 보안 커뮤니티 전반과 공유할 것을 약속했다.

AI 시대는 소프트웨어를 제공하는 모든 조직이 감당해야 할 위험 부담을 한층 키우고 있다. 공격자들은 대다수 보안 툴이 대응하도록 설계된 속도보다 더 빠르게 취약점을 악용하고 있다. 프론티어 AI 모델은 이제 기존 스캐닝 방식으로는 발견하지 못했던 위험, 즉 수년간 코드베이스에 잠재해 있던 유형의 위험까지 찾아낼 수 있는 수준에 이르렀다.

태니엄은 이러한 역량의 발전을 지속적으로 주시하며 이미 범용 AI 모델을 자사 코드베이스에 활용해 왔다. 이번 프로젝트 글래스윙 참여를 계기로, 태니엄은 클로드 미토스를 통해 취약점 연구 역량을 한층 강화할 수 있게 됐다.

태니엄의 크리스천 헌트(Christian Hunt) 최고 엔지니어링 책임자(Chief Engineering Officer)는 "태니엄이 출시하는 모든 코드 한 줄 한 줄은 IT 및 보안 운영자들이 가장 중요한 시스템을 보호하기 위해 신뢰하는 코드"라며 "태니엄은 고객을 안전하게 지키겠다는 약속을 진지하게 이행하고 있다. 프로젝트 글래스윙은 프론티어 AI 역량에 대한 접근권을 제공, 우리에게 의존하는 조직들이 피해를 입기 전에 취약점을 찾아내고 수정할 수 있게 해준다"고 말했다.

태니엄은 금융기관, 헬스케어 시스템, 정부기관을 포함해 전 세계 최대 규모의 고객사들을 지원하고 있다. 이러한 규모의 조직에게 태니엄 소프트웨어의 보안 수준은 곧 그들 자신의 보안 태세로 직결된다. 프로젝트 글래스윙 참여는 태니엄이 고객의 보안 환경을 지킬 때와 동일한 수준의 엄격함을 자사 코드에도 적용하겠다는 의지를 보여준다.

태니엄은 프로젝트가 진행됨에 따라 워크플로우, 트리아지(Triage, 선별) 방식, 그리고 프론티어 AI가 효과적인 코드 보안의 기준을 어떻게 바꾸고 있는지에 대해 얻은 인사이트를 보안 커뮤니티를 위해 공개할 예정이다. 또한 태니엄은 CVE 번호 부여 기관 (CVE Numbering Authority, CNA)으로서의 의무를 계속 이행하며, 자사 제품의 취약점에 대한 CVE 기록과 보안 권고문을 발행할 계획이다.

한편 태니엄은 자율형 IT(Autonomous IT) 기업이다. AI가 혁신과 리스크를 동시에 가속화하는 가운데, 태니엄의 자율 운영 체제인 태니엄 아틀라스(Tanium Atlas)는 인간과 에이전트를 막론한 모든 IT 및 보안 운영자에게 태니엄 자율형 IT 플랫폼의 모든 역량을 온전히 제공한다. 태니엄은 엔드포인트 자산 전반에서 머신 속도로 위협을 탐지·판단·대응할 수 있도록, 실시간 인텔리전스와 에이전트 기반 의사결정, 자율 실행 역량을 운영자에게 제공한다. 2026년 가트너 엔드포인트 관리 툴 부문 첫 매직 쿼드런트에서 리더로 선정됐다. 또 IDC 마켓스케이프의 '2025~2026 전 세계 클라이언트 엔드포인트 관리 소프트웨어(Windows 디바이스 관리) 부문 벤더 평가'에서도 리더로, '포레스터 웨이브(The Forrester Wave™): 엔드포인트 관리 플랫폼, 2026년 2분기' 평가에서도 리더로 각각 선정됐다.

items.title: Apple’s clever software solution lets iPhone batteries skirt shipping limits
items.summary: Apple has developed an unexpected workaround to prevent the iPhone 18 Pro Max from being hit by shipping restrictions on big batteries. There's a "battery-firmware solution" in place on the new iPhones, according to Apple's support page, which keeps capacity below the 20Wh limit
items.content:
﻿The iPhone 18 Pro Max removes its 20Wh firmware lock upon user activation.

Apple has developed an unexpected workaround to prevent the iPhone 18 Pro Max from being hit by shipping restrictions on big batteries. There’s a “battery-firmware solution” in place on the new iPhones, according to Apple’s support page , which keeps capacity below the 20Wh limit for single-cell batteries set by international shipping regulations — but this firmware lock automatically removes itself when the device is booted up for the first time.

Following user activation, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is restored to its original rated charging capacity, which is around 21.75Wh for US eSIM-only models and 21.06Wh for European models with a physical SIM slot. If the user needs to send off their phone for repair or resale, the charging limitation can be restored using the “Prepare to Ship” feature, which caps charging to 80 percent for 14 days. The restoration feature can be found under the settings menu by opening General settings, tapping Transfer or Reset iPhone, and then Prepare to Ship.

Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro Max battery “might need to discharge for Prepare to Ship to complete,” and may become warmer than usual during the process. Prepare to Ship can be disabled at any time by heading back into the settings menu.

It’s a novel way to circumvent the battery capacity limits as phone makers continue to chase longer battery life while shrinking devices. By comparison, Android manufacturers generally tend to ship their devices with smaller, dual-cell batteries outside Asia to get around the same shipping restrictions, but those solutions are costlier and less efficient in terms of physical space. If Apple’s firmware fix pans out, we may see Android manufacturers offering a similar solution.

items.content:
최정의 글로벌사업본부장 "2년 연속 부스 마련...동남아 시장 공략 가속"

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/09/21 21:31

AI 네이티브 보안 플랫폼 기업 안랩(대표 강석균)이 지난 15일부터 16일까지 인도네시아 자카르타에서 열린 현지 대표 사이버 보안 전시회 ‘인도섹 2026(Indosec 2026)’에 참가했다.

'인도섹'은 공공·금융을 타깃으로 한 인도네시아 최대 규모 보안 행사다. 안랩은 올해 2년 연속 참가했다. 자사 통합 브랜드 ‘안랩 AI 플러스’를 중심으로 보안 운영을 지능화하는 다양한 솔루션을 선보였다.

안랩은 "행사 기간 동안 대기업, 금융 IT, 제조, 광업 등 다양한 현지 산업 관계자 400여 명이 전시 부스를 방문해 안랩 AI 플러스를 체험하고 협력 방안을 논의했다"고 밝혔다. 이어 "참관객들은 AI가 단순히 위협을 요약하거나 특정 보안 업무를 자동화하는 수준을 넘어, 위협 분석부터 대응으로 이어지는 보안 운영 과정을 지능화한다는 점에 주목했다"고 덧붙였다.

안랩 EDR은 복수의 AI 에이전트가 탐지된 위협을 분석해 공격 의도와 맥락, 대응 방향을 보고서 형태로 제공한다. 이때 안랩이 보유한 방대한 보안 데이터 중 유관 정보를 종합해 위협의 맥락과 의미를 제시한다. 이에, 보안 담당자가 복잡한 위협 정보를 빠르게 이해하고 대응 방법을 판단할 수 있도록 한다는 점이 호응을 얻었다고 회사는 설명했다.

이외에도 SaaS형 위협 분석 플랫폼 ‘안랩 XDR’, IT-OT 융합 사이버물리시스템(CPS) 보안 플랫폼 ‘안랩 CPS 플러스’, 차세대 위협 인텔리전스 플랫폼 ‘안랩 TIP’, 샌드박스 기반 지능형 위협 대응 솔루션 ‘안랩 MDS’ 등 다양한 영역을 아우르는 플랫폼과 솔루션을 출품했다.

최정의 안랩 글로벌사업본부장은 “AI가 사이버 위협 패러다임을 바꾸면서 AI를 활용한 보안 운영 지능화는 동남아를 비롯한 전 세계 고객의 공통 과제”라며 “국내는 물론 일본, 중국, 중동 등 글로벌 시장에서 축적한 기술과 고객 경험을 바탕으로 안랩 AI 플러스의 경쟁력을 인도네시아 등 동남아 시장에 알려 나가겠다”고 말했다.

한편, 안랩은 올 5월 대만 ‘사이버섹’, 7월 말레이시아 ‘NCSS’ 등 동남아 주요 보안 행사에 참여하며 현지 고객과의 접점을 넓히고 있다. 오는 10월에는 싱가포르의 대규모 IT 전시회 ‘가브웨어 2026(Govware 2026)’에 참여, 동남아 사업에 박차를 가할 예정이다.

한편 '안랩 AI플러스(AhnLab AI PLUS)'는 안랩의 AI-네이티브 보안 전략과 방향성을 대표하는 통합 브랜드이자, 기술·제품·서비스를 유기적으로 연결하는 플랫폼 및 아키텍처 개념이다. 제품·영역별로 분산된 데이터를 하나의 보안 맥락으로 연결하고, 복수의 AI 에이전트가 협업해 보안 운영과정을 수행하는 에이전틱 AI 기반 아키텍처를 지향한다.

맥킨지 조사 대기업 40% AI 확장 단계 진입…수익성 입증 과제 대두

인터넷 입력 :2026/09/21 21:09

애피어가 에이전틱 AI의 비즈니스 성과를 지속해서 확대하기 위해 기업이 갖춰야 할 5가지 핵심 조건인 '스케일'(SCALE)을 새롭게 제시했다.

21일 회사에 따르면, 최근 맥킨지가 발표한 '2026 AI 현황' 조사 결과 연 매출 10억 달러 이상 대기업 중 AI 에이전트를 확장 단계에서 활용한다는 응답은 지난해 27%에서 올해 40%로 급증했다. 반면 AI 활용이 수익성 개선에 기여했다고 답한 비율은 37%로 전년과 비슷한 수준에 머물렀다. 이에 애피어는 기업의 AI 활용이 본격적인 확장 단계에 접어든 만큼 논의의 초점을 단순한 기술 도입에서 실제 업무에서의 운영과 성과 확대로 전환해야 한다고 진단했다.

애피어가 제시한 핵심 조건 스케일은 5가지 실무 지침의 영문 앞 글자를 딴 개념이다. 첫 번째는 '전략적 목표 설정(Strategic)'으로, 매출 성장이나 비용 절감 등 명확하고 측정 가능한 비즈니스 목표를 수립하는 단계다. 두 번째 '역량 및 한계 판단(Calibrated)'은 AI가 스스로 확신 수준을 평가하고 잠재적 위험을 고려해 행동 여부를 결정하는 능력을 뜻하며, 주요 업무 흐름마다 점검과 안전장치 적용이 필수적이다.

이어 세 번째 '적응형 운영(Adaptive)'은 과업의 목적과 난이도에 맞춰 적합한 모델과 에이전트를 선택하고 조율하는 과정을 말한다. 네 번째 '지속적 학습(Learning)'은 축적되는 맥락과 사용자 피드백을 이후 판단에 반영해 일회성 자동화를 넘어서는 가치를 창출하는 단계다. 마지막 '효율적 자원 활용(Efficient)'은 거대언어모델(LLM)의 토큰 최적화 등을 통해 연산 자원을 낭비 없이 적절히 투입하는 것을 핵심으로 한다. 애피어는 이러한 연구와 기술 역량을 자사 제품에 적용해 기업이 AI 투자를 실질적인 성과(ROI)로 전환하도록 지원하고 있다.

치한 위 애피어 CEO 겸 공동창업자는 “이제 기업의 관심은 도입한 AI가 어떤 성과를 내고 있으며, 이를 어떻게 지속적으로 확대할 수 있을지에 집중되고 있다”며 “에이전틱 AI가 더 많은 판단과 실행을 맡게 될수록 자율성 자체보다 이를 얼마나 신뢰할 수 있고 효율적으로 운영하느냐가 중요해진다. 결국 AI의 자율성이 높아질수록 이를 운영하는 기업의 판단 역시 더 정교해져야 한다”고 말했다.

경영분야 AI에이전트까지 3개 사업 수행…공공 AX 실증 모델 본격화

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/09/21 21:06

AI·빅데이터 플랫폼 전문기업 티쓰리큐(대표 박병훈)가 한국도로공사의 생성형 AI 서비스 고도화와 안정적 운영을 위한 사업 수행에 본격 착수했다. 지난 15일 한국도로공사 회의실에서 'RoADi 고도화 용역 및 2026~2027년 RoADi 서비스' 유지관리 용역 착수보고회를 개최했다.

티쓰리큐는 이번 2개 사업에 앞서 ‘경영분야 AI Agent 구축’ 사업도 수주해 수행 중이다. 이에 따라 한국도로공사의 생성형 AI 서비스인 'RoADi'를 중심으로 업무 특화 AI 에이전트 구축, 생성형 AI 서비스 고도화, 운영·품질관리를 아우르는 3개 사업을 동시에 추진하게 됐다.

'RoADi 고도화 사업'은 한국도로공사 내·외부 규정과 업무자료를 학습한 언어모델의 기능과 학습영역을 확장해 임직원 업무 효율을 높이는 것을 목표로 한다. 주요 과업은 기존 학습데이터 최신화, 내부방침·보도자료 등 신규 데이터 반영, 업무영역별 RAG 구성, 멀티모달 기반 파서 도입, 이미지 검색 및 STT 기능 고도화, 최신 LLM과 전문 AI 모델 적용 환경 구성 등이다.

특히 감사, 국회, 재무, 안전, 건설기술, 기술마켓, 재난대응, ex피디아, 구조물 유지관리, 민원응대 등 다양한 업무 분야별 특화 기능을 확장해 RoADi를 단순 질의응답 시스템에서 업무 수행형 AI Agent 플랫폼으로 발전시키는 데 초점을 둔다.

유지관리 사업은 RoADi 서비스의 안정적 운영과 품질 개선을 위한 체계적 관리가 핵심이다. 티쓰리큐는 서비스 상태 모니터링, 장애 대응, AI 모델 및 프롬프트 최적화, RAG 및 학습데이터 관리, 벤치마크 데이터셋 기반 품질 측정, 사용자 피드백 분석 등을 수행하며, RoADi가 실제 업무 환경에서 지속적으로 활용될 수 있게 운영 안정성과 답변 품질을 함께 관리할 계획이다.

티쓰리큐는 이번 사업에 자사의 DX/AX 전주기 공통플랫폼 EDPP(Enterprise Data Processing Platform) 기반 기술과 AI에이전트 개발 방법론을 적용한다. EDPP는 데이터 수집, 변환, 적재, 검색, 분석, 생성형 AI 활용, 운영관리를 하나의 체계로 연결하는 플랫폼이다. RAG, 그래프 RAG, 하이브리드 온톨로지, Private LLM, 멀티모달 처리, 에이전트 오케스트레이션(Agent Orchestration) 등을 결합해 기관별 업무에 맞는 AI 서비스를 빠르게 구현하고 안정적으로 운영할 수 있게 지원한다.

박병훈 티쓰리큐 대표는 “이제 공공과 기업 모두 AX의 초입을 지나 본격적인 AI 활용 시대로 진입하고 있다”며 “사일로 형태로 데이터를 쌓아두는 시대는 끝났고, 중요한 것은 플랫폼 위에서 얼마나 쉽고 빠르게 AI 서비스를 만들고, 얼마나 잘 운영하느냐”라고 말했다. 이어 “티쓰리큐는 단순히 플랫폼을 공급하는 데 그치지 않고, AI에이전트 개발 8단계 방법론, R&D와 현업이 결합된 수행조직, DX/AX 풀라이프사이클 엔지니어 양성 체계를 함께 제공해 고객기관의 AI 전환이 실제 성과로 이어지도록 지원하고자 한다”며 “한국도로공사 RoADi 사업은 말로만 이야기되는 K-팔란티어가 아니라, 대한민국 공공 AX 현장에서 검증되는 실증 사례가 될 것”이라고 강조했다.

티쓰리큐는 이번 한국도로공사 3개 사업 수행을 통해 공공기관의 생성형 AI 도입이 단순 챗봇이나 검색 기능을 넘어, 데이터 기반 의사결정과 업무 자동화, 지속적 운영관리 체계로 확장되는 대표 사례를 만들 계획이다. 이를 기반으로 향후 B2B 및 타 공공기관으로 AI에이전트 기반 DX/AX 플랫폼 적용을 확대하고, 대한민국형 엔터프라이즈 AI 플랫폼 기업으로 성장해 나간다는 방침이다.

items.title: 4 ways to address the failures we found along the US border’s “virtual wall”
items.summary: MIT Technology Review today published our investigation into how many people have died near the “virtual wall” of surveillance towers that the US government has installed along the US-Mexico border. We found cases of people who walked undetected through areas surveilled by advanc
items.content:
MIT Technology Review today published our investigation into how many people have died near the “virtual wall” of surveillance towers that the US government has installed along the US-Mexico border.

We found cases of people who walked undetected through areas surveilled by advanced, AI-enabled towers and later died nearby, where their bodies remained unnoticed for weeks or months. These cases reflect systemic flaws in the virtual wall: broken towers, algorithms that failed to detect people, and agents who simply did not respond to alerts.

This story is part of Dying on Camera , a collaboration between MIT Technology Review and Times of San Diego . Journalists in both newsrooms spent the past year examining the failures of border surveillance technology and uncovering the stories of the people who die in the borderlands .

Each of these deaths should have raised alarms inside US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) about the flaws in the agency’s surveillance network. This is particularly true for cases near the latest towers built by the defense company Anduril, which continues to win major contracts and is poised to benefit from the windfall of federal money slated for border security. The US is set to spend $1 billion to triple the size of the virtual wall by 2034.

Here are four ideas for what CBP should do next to address these failures.

“If I were the federal government, I would do an audit, because this feels like it’s not working.”

That was New Mexico state representative Sarah Silva’s reaction when MIT Technology Review showed her that in 2024 alone, more than 18 people had died near surveillance towers in just one small stretch of desert near her district.

An audit is necessary because, despite poring over thousands of pages of police reports and other documents about surveillance towers, we have only limited knowledge of how many towers are out there and where they’re located.

CBP does not publish a comprehensive map of its virtual wall. We instead relied on mapping work led by the nonprofit Electronic Frontier Foundation and then used satellite imagery to verify where specific towers were and approximately when they were installed.

We analyzed lots of towers—nearly 600. But that’s still far less than the 800 the government says operate today. And our estimates of when they went up are inexact. That means our tally of more than 1,050 people who have died near them is an undercount. And we don’t have a complete picture of where along the border the problem is worst.

An internal audit would not have such limitations. In theory, CBP tracks when each tower went up and when it was active. It has had the ability to audit their effectiveness—while quantifying how many people have died near them—since at least 2015, when it began installing the types of towers included in our analysis. But sources told us it has never done such an audit. Our findings make the need for one more urgent.

If CBP is to analyze instances where people have died near its surveillance technology, it needs to know when and where those deaths happen. And the current system for tracking that data is beyond broken.

As we note in our methodology , there is no national agency that collects and publishes all available records on migrant deaths. We sifted through thousands of pages of records from dozens of agencies in Texas alone, and our picture is still incomplete owing to the lack of a shared protocol for documenting these deaths in public records.

Border Patrol has had its own internal system, called the Border Safety Initiative Tracking System (BSITS), in place since 2007. But it wasn't until 2021 that national rules were established for how different sectors should enter cases into the system. The next year, the Government Accountability Office (GAO) found that many cases still weren't being tracked in this system, especially deaths that weren't discovered by Border Patrol. In 2023, the GAO reported that Border Patrol has taken steps to fix that, but outside researchers consistently find the agency’s estimates to be undercounts even today.

In addition to tracking migrant deaths, CBP launched a program in 2017 to prevent them, called the Missing Migrant Program. In April 2025, the GAO found the program was improving the way it collected and tracked data about events like 911 calls and rescues. The problem, it said, was that there was no plan in place to use the data to measure whether the program was actually increasing rescues or reducing deaths, which are its primary goals. It made two recommendations for solutions, neither of which has been implemented.

In 2014, when the virtual wall was much smaller, the GAO suggested that Border Patrol agents log when a piece of technology helped them apprehend someone who was trying to enter the US illegally. It would take agents some extra time, but logging these assists would help Congress understand how often various surveillance technologies were leading to actual apprehensions. Once this data was collected, GAO added, the agency should measure whether its surveillance technologies were working. CBP agreed, and it started requiring agents to enter such information.

Then, in 2017, the GAO reported that the data being collected was inaccurate and unreliable; it found agents in Texas, for example, who were crediting a specific type of tower in apprehensions hundreds of times, even though no such towers existed anywhere in the state. Border Patrol again said it would improve; it agreed to train agents on the importance of collecting such information.

But years later, agents told us, it’s still not a priority. One former CBP official described the mandate as “spitting in the wind, to be honest,” and said the messy reality of apprehensions doesn't translate into neat metrics. (The official, who requested anonymity, served during the Biden administration and wasn’t authorized to discuss sensitive issues.)

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/09/21 20:59

스페이스XAI가 음성을 텍스트로 바꾸는 모델 '그록 보이스 트랜스크라이브 2.0'을 공개했다. 스페이스XAI 공식 블로그에 따르면 이 모델은 실사용 환경 평가에서 1.0 버전보다 두 배 정확하며 가격은 동일하다.

2.0 버전은 그록 보이스의 기반이 된 오디오 파운데이션 모델 위에서 개발됐다. 그록 보이스는 하루 수만 건의 고객 지원 통화와 수백만 시간 분량의 영상 내레이션을 처리하고, 테슬라 차량의 그록 어시스턴트를 포함한 물리 제품의 음성 에이전트로도 운영된다. 훈련에는 실시간이면서 잡음이 많은 다국어 오디오 데이터가 사용됐다.

공개 벤치마크인 아티피셜 애널리시스 리더보드에서 스트리밍 모델 32종 중 정확도 1위를 기록했다. 회사는 고객 지원 통화의 전화 음성, 그록과의 대화, 계정 코드나 이메일 주소 같은 음성 자격 증명, 19개 언어의 짧은 음성 명령을 내부 평가 항목으로 삼았고 모두 1.0보다 개선됐다고 밝혔다. 전화 음성에서는 시험한 모든 모델보다 정확도가 높았다.

차량 내 명령 같은 짧은 발화에서는 단어 오류율(WER)이 20.6%에서 6.8%로 낮아졌다. 짧은 구문 인식의 개선 폭이 가장 컸다. 단어 오류율은 받아쓴 결과에서 틀린 단어의 비율이다. 다국어 정확도도 1.0 대비 크게 개선됐으며, 수십 개 언어를 지원하고 언어를 자동으로 감지해 녹음 중간에 언어가 바뀌어도 한 번에 처리한다.

이 모델은 배치·스트리밍 변환과 단어 단위 타임스탬프, 화자 분리, 최대 100개 키워드 바이어싱, 8채널 멀티채널, 필러 단어 제거, 스마트 턴 감지를 지원한다. 타임스탬프에는 신뢰도 점수가 함께 제공된다. 산찬 색세나 아틀라시안 팀워크 컬렉션 부사장은 룸(Loom) 영상에서 이 모델이 기존 방식보다 정확하다고 평가했다. 가격은 배치 기준 오디오 1시간당 0.10달러, 스트리밍 기준 0.20달러로 1.0과 같다.

그록 보이스 트랜스크라이브 2.0은 곧 음성-텍스트 API의 기본 모델이 된다. 1.0 버전은 수주 안에 지원이 종료되며, 전환 기간에 1.0을 계속 쓰려면 모델 ID를 grok-voice-transcribe-1.0으로 고정하면 된다.

자세한 내용은 스페이스XAI(SpaceXAI) 에서 확인할 수 있다.

items.content:
"한국인 창업가 강점과 실리콘밸리 혁신 생태계 연결할 것”

인터넷 입력 :2026/09/21 20:58

글로벌 스타트업 액셀러레이션 기업 누립이 중소벤처기업부와 창업진흥원이 주관하는 ‘모두의 창업 글로벌’ 재외국민 프로그램의 실리콘밸리 현지 운영을 담당한다.

21일 누립에 따르면, 이번 ‘실리콘밸리 K-컬처 콘텐츠 트랙’은 해외 거주 한국 국적의 예비창업자 및 7년 이내 창업기업을 대상으로 진행된다. K-뷰티·푸드·패션·엔터테인먼트·미디어·게임·소비재·웰니스 및 관련 AI·기술 분야 스타트업 15개사를 선발해 약 4주간 실리콘밸리 현지에서 실전형 액셀러레이팅을 운영한다. 선발 기업에는 현지 시장 분석, GTM(Go-to-Market) 전략 고도화, 멘토링, 파트너 발굴 등의 혜택과 함께 예비창업자 최대 2000만원, 창업기업 최대 3000만원의 창업활동비가 지원된다.

누립은 현지 네트워크와 액셀러레이션 역량을 토대로 참가 기업이 미국 시장과 창업 생태계를 직접 경험하고 실질적인 비즈니스 기회를 발굴하도록 밀착 지원할 방침이다.

도유선 누립 이사는 “이번 프로그램의 목표는 재외국민 창업가를 단순히 실리콘밸리에 데려오는 것이 아니다”라며 “실제 미국 시장에서 고객과 파트너를 만나고 현지 전문가 및 창업 생태계와 연결되면서 미국 시장에서 지속적으로 사업을 확장할 수 있는 기반을 만드는 것이 핵심”이라고 말했다.

이어 “해외에서 이미 현지 시장을 경험하고 네트워크를 구축한 한국인 창업가들의 강점과 실리콘밸리의 혁신 생태계를 연결해 한국인 창업가가 글로벌 시장에서 새로운 비즈니스 기회를 만들어낼 수 있도록 현지에서 밀도 있게 지원하겠다”고 약속했다.
